The whole of [Harmony](elements-harmony.qmd) on one sheet. Every ▶ plays the example; the cadences play with chords. Press **Full screen** to put the sheet on the whole screen for
revision or for the class board.

## The sheet

::::::: {.el-sheet .column-page data-title="Harmony: chords and keys"}
:::::: {.el-grid}

::::: {.el-card}
#### Key signatures
<p>The sharps or flats at the start of each line. Each major key shares one with its <strong>relative minor</strong>, three [half steps]{.nn} lower.</p>
<ul><li>none: C / A minor</li><li>1♯: G / E minor</li><li>2♯: D / B minor</li><li>1♭: F / D minor</li><li>2♭: B♭ / G minor</li></ul>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Major
<p>Often sounds bright. Look at the last note and chord: usually the tonic.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
"C"E G c G|"G"D B, "C"C2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Minor
<p>Often darker. The same signature as its relative major, plus the raised 7th (here G♯).</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="96"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:Am
"Am"A, C E C|"E"E ^G, "Am"A,2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Modal, pentatonic, atonal
<ul>
<li><strong>Modal</strong>: built on an older scale (Dorian, Mixolydian…)</li>
<li><strong>Pentatonic</strong>: five notes, C D E G A (heard here)</li>
<li><strong>Atonal</strong>: no key, no home note</li></ul>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/8
K:C
E2 G2 A2 G2|E2 D2 C4|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Modulation
<p>A change of key mid-piece: often to the dominant or the relative minor; in pop, the last chorus up a step.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="100"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
"C"E G "G"D C|[K:D]"D"F A "A"E D|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Triads
<p>Three notes a 3rd apart: root, 3rd, 5th. Numbered I–vii°: capitals major, small letters minor. In C: I C, ii Dm, IV F, V G, vi Am.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="72"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
"I"[CEG]2 "IV"[FAc]2|"V"[GBd]2 "I"[CEG]2|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Sevenths and beyond
<p>Another 3rd on top makes a <strong>seventh</strong> (G7 = G B D F); more make <strong>extended chords</strong> (9ths, 11ths), common in jazz.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="70"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/4
K:C
"G"[GBd]2 "G7"[GBdf]2|"G9"[GBdfa]4|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### [Authentic cadence]{.nn}
<p>V → I. Finished: a full stop.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="80" data-style="hymn"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:C
"C"E "F"F|"G"D "C"C|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Plagal cadence
<p>IV → I. Finished, softer: the "Amen" of hymns.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="80" data-style="hymn"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:C
"C"E "G"D|"F"C "C"C|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### [Half cadence]{.nn}
<p>Anything → V. Unfinished: a comma, or a question.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="80" data-style="hymn"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:C
"C"E "F"F|"C"E "G"D|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### [Deceptive cadence]{.nn}
<p>V → vi (usually). A surprise: you expect I and get a minor chord.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="80" data-style="hymn"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:C
"C"E "F"F|"G"D "Am"C|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card}
#### Picardy third
<p>A minor-key piece that ends on a <strong>major</strong> tonic chord.</p>
<div class="abc-ex" data-width="190" data-bpm="76" data-style="hymn"><script type="text/plain">
X:1
M:4/4
L:1/2
K:Dm
"Dm"F "Gm"G|"A"E "D"^F|]
</script></div>
:::::

::::: {.el-card .el-wide}
#### Check yourself
<div class="eq" data-set="harmony"></div>
:::::

::::::
:::::::

## Describing harmony

- Say the tonality first (major, minor, modal…), then anything that changes: a modulation, a Picardy third at the end.
- The cadence names follow the **British note names** switch: *perfect*, *imperfect* and *interrupted* are the British
  *authentic*, *half* and *deceptive*.

- The longer lesson, with fuller examples: [Elements 3: Harmony and Tonality](elements-harmony.qmd).
